final_answer.long_answer: Reference: [GG_1], [GG_2], [GG_7]. Detailed explanation based on the information: The provided context indicates that in Type I xanthinuria there is an isolated deficiency of xanthine dehydrogenase (also called xanthine oxidase), which is the enzyme responsible for converting xanthine into uric acid – a key breakdown product in purine nucleotide metabolism. This enzyme deficiency results in the accumulation of xanthine, leading to the clinical manifestations of Type I xanthinuria.
